theorem_final.theorem_title: The bridge: Problem 97 implies the 3n bound and Problem 96
theorem_final.formal_statement:
theorem Erdos9796Mission.linear_bound_of_problem97 :
    Problem97 → (∀ A : Finset Plane, ConvexIndep (A : Set Plane) → unitDistancePairsCount A ≤ 3 * A.card) ∧ Problem96 := by sorry
theorem_final.natural_language_statement:
Assume the affirmative statement of Erdős Problem 97 for every nonempty finite convex-independent point set in the Euclidean plane. Then every finite convex-independent set $A$, including the empty set, satisfies

$$u(A)\le3|A|,$$

and the extremal function satisfies

$$U_c(n)=O(n).$$

Here $u(A)$ counts unordered pairs of distinct points at distance one, each pair once, and $U_c(n)$ is the supremum of these counts over convex-independent n-point sets. Both conclusions are required. This is a conditional theorem, with Problem 97 as an explicit hypothesis. The repository records the conditional peeling proof and the subsequent supremum-to-Big-O step; transferring both makes the complete link between the two mission targets reusable.

readback.readback: Assume that every nonempty finite set $C$ of points in the real Euclidean plane whose points all lie outside the real convex hull of the remaining points fails to have the following property: for every $p\in C$ there is a positive real radius $r>0$ such that $\{q\in C : \operatorname{dist}(p,q)=r\}$ has cardinality at least $4$. Then both of the following hold: for every finite set $A$ of plane points satisfying the same convex-hull condition, including the possibility that $A$ is empty, the number $\operatorname{unitDistancePairsCount}(A)$ of unordered two-element pairs from $A$ counted once, where a pair $\{p,q\}$ is counted exactly when $0<\operatorname{dist}(p,q)$ and $\operatorname{dist}(p,q)=1$, is at most $3|A|$; and the real-valued function sending $n$ to the natural-number supremum of these unit-distance counts over finite convex-independent point sets of cardinality $n$ grows as $O(n)$ along natural numbers tending to infinity.

milestone_final.title: The bridge: Problem 97 implies the 3n bound and Problem 96
milestone_final.milestone_description:
**Server-verified conditional bridge.** Assuming Problem 97, every finite convex-independent planar set A has at most 3|A| unordered unit-distance pairs. Taking the supremum over n-point sets gives Problem 96 with explicit constant three.

The proof deletes a vertex of unit degree at most three and counts unordered pairs directly in the symmetric square. Problem 97 remains an explicit hypothesis; this milestone does not settle either original problem unconditionally.

[Verified proof](https://prove2.me/theorems/d76e105d-be12-48ae-8965-782674afd985)
